title: Kalanj
eyebrow: Anna's people, and the parish nobody has opened
dek: The family this archive's own great-great-grandmother came from — what can be proved about her, what two archives disagreed about, and the parish register that would answer it. The Kalanj genealogy proper is kept in The Blažević Archive; this page is the join, and the evidence on this side of it.
lead: David asked on 29 September 2026 whether Kalanj was a family this site should track and give a page to. It was, and building it found a misreading this archive had carried in fifteen files.

rows.lab: The join: Anna Kalanj, born 3 January 1864
rows.text: Entry 2 of 1864 in the baptismal register of Ledenice, the Vinodol parish above Crikvenica: «Anna, legitima — Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» — at «Kljenovica N° 22». Godparents Josephus Ban and his wife Anna; baptised by Vincentius Segulja, parish priest. She married Josip Defranceschi, the stonecutter's son who brought this archive's line down from Gračišće to the coast, and she is generation four of the direct line. (doc — the plate is held here.)

rows.lab: ⚠ «Rijenovica» does not exist, and the mistake hid a fact
rows.text: Until today this archive read that place as «Rijenovica house 22» and said so in fifteen files, including the pedigree's own wall note. There is no Rijenovica: the word returns zero hits in this archive's Croatian gazetteer. The register says KLJENOVICA — the older spelling of Klenovica — and the Blažević Archive has read it correctly all along. What the misreading concealed: this site's Crikvenica page already says «House 22 is somewhere in this line of roofs — Anton Rudolf Defranceski was born in it on 20 January 1890.» Anna was born in the SAME HOUSE twenty-six years earlier. The archive held «house 22» at both ends and never joined them. The correction is on /corrections/.

rows.lab: ⚠ And the entry says where they came from: BRINJE
rows.text: «Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» — country people of the parish of Brinje. No file of this archive carried that phrase, and it is the most important thing in the entry: the Kalanj were not coastal people. Brinje is inland, up behind the Velebit gap, and they had come down to Klenovica on the shore. The Blažević Archive calls Brinje «the single largest hole in this family» and records that «not one page of its register has been opened». So both archives now stand at the same closed door, and this page exists partly to say so.

rows.lab: The oldest open question here is a Kalanj question
rows.text: The registers name ANA KALANJ in all four Crikvenica baptismal entries of her children. The family's own genealogy gives Josip a wife ANA GRUBIŠIĆ, 19 September 1863 – 28 May 1936, and that is the name cut on the Crikvenica gravestone. The registers govern and the stone is unexplained — and the stone no longer exists, because the plot was sold and the monument taken apart, so the photograph of it is now the only record. This is why Anna's page carries no death date: the only date on offer belongs to a name this archive cannot yet reconcile with hers.

rows.lab: The stones, and one of them is a question
rows.text: Five Kalanj monuments were photographed in the cemeteries of Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski and Klenovica on 29 September 2026 and are held here as plates. ⚠ LUKA KALANJ 1859–1944 and KATA 1860–1942 were born five and four years before Anna, in the same small stretch of the Vinodol. A brother is the obvious guess and a guess is all it is: Anna's father was Josip, and no stone names a father. The Ledenice baptisms of the 1850s would settle it in an afternoon. The others: Albert 1895–1945 with five more of his household; Petar 1913–1971 and Vera 1917–2011 with the infant Milan 1943–1944; Mate 1928–1992; Franjo 1933–2004; and a joint Kalanj–Rebrović stone. A sixth, LOVRO 1906–1965 with Ana, Ivan and Marijan, was photographed but did not reach this archive as a file.

rows.lab: Where this page stops, and why
rows.text: The Kalanj genealogy proper — 215 published people, earliest birth 1734, running through Klenovica and Povile — is kept in The Blažević Archive, and is not rebuilt here. That boundary is right, and it had one cost that this page is the answer to: while each archive read only its own page, the two of them held one baptism and disagreed about the village for months. What belongs HERE is the join, the evidence photographed on this side, and the disagreements between the two. What belongs THERE is the family.

source_kalanj: Ledenice baptismal register, entry 2 of 1864, read from the plate held here at 6×. David's photographs of the Kalanj graves, 29 September 2026. The Blažević Archive's Kalanj page, read 29 September 2026.
